description_full: Safe Bulkers, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides marine drybulk transportation services internationally. The company owns and operates a fleet of dry bulk vessels for transporting bulk cargoes comprising coal, grain, and iron ore. Its fleet consists of 45 vessels, including 8 Panamax class vessels, 12 Kamsarmax class vessels, 17 post-Panamax class vessels, and 8 Capesize class vessels with an aggregate carrying capacity of 4,559,000 deadweight tons. Safe Bulkers, Inc. was incorporated in 2007 and is based in Monaco.
ceo_bio: Mr. Polys  Hajioannou | Chairman & CEO | Age 58
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 10 people. Stock-based compensation of $15K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Safe Bulkers, Inc is a small-cap industrials business with a $809M market cap.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 44% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
